# ask-a-human

> ask-a-human is one copy-paste MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets an AI agent pause and
> ask a human for approval — on their phone. The human approves, declines, picks an option, or types a
> reply, and the agent receives exactly that decision. Approvals are end-to-end encrypted: the relay in
> the middle is content-blind — it only ever forwards `base64(nonce‖ciphertext)` plus which room talks to
> which, so it cannot read decision contents or forge a signed decision. It can observe metadata,
> record ciphertext, and delay or drop delivery. No accounts or relay database.

How it works: the MCP server runs locally next to your agent over stdio. On the first `request_approval`
it prints a short code to stderr; you type it into the app on your phone to pair over a Magic-Wormhole-style
SPAKE2 handshake — an in-house, RFC 9382-style construction in which a short pairing code becomes a strong
shared key. After that, each approval is sealed with NaCl secretbox on one side and opened on the other.
The relay in between sees only `base64(nonce‖ciphertext)` and which room talks to which — never the
content, never the decision.

## Add it to your agent (zero setup)

Paste this into your MCP client config — Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`), Claude Desktop
(`claude_desktop_config.json`), Codex, or any MCP client:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ask-a-human": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@askahuman/mcp", "serve"] } } }
```

No account, no API key, nothing to configure. `npx` fetches a single static release binary on first run
and defaults to the hosted relay `wss://ask-a-human.ai/ws` and PWA `https://ask-a-human.ai`. To self-host,
pass `--relay <wss-url>` and `--web <https-origin>`.

## Tools

- `request_approval` — Ask a human to approve/decline/answer on their phone. BLOCKS until the human
  responds or it times out. A failure, decline, or timeout is NEVER returned as approved. Inputs:
  - `title` (string, required) — short title shown on the phone card.
  - `summary` (string, required) — the human-readable question body.
  - `response_kind` (string, required) — answer shape: `yesno` | `choice` | `text`.
  - `category` (string, optional) — badge; recognized values `cash` | `deploy` | `data` | `access` |
    `other`. Any other value is accepted and simply shown as `other` (not rejected).
  - `options` (string[], optional) — the choices, when `response_kind` is `choice`.
  - `placeholder` (string, optional) — input hint, when `response_kind` is `text`.
  - `max_len` (integer, optional) — text limit in Unicode scalar values, 0–4096; 0/omitted defaults to 4096.
  - `expires_in_s` (integer, optional) — request lifetime, 0–86400 seconds; 0/omitted adds no timeout. Caller deadlines still apply.
- `pair_status` — Report whether a pairing session exists, the phone's relay presence, or waiting/idle status. Read-only; returns only
  non-secret status (the pairing code is shown out-of-band in the terminal, never in the result). It
  does not start pairing.
- `start_pairing` — Begin pairing in the background and show the code in the agent terminal.
  An ordinary call preserves existing sessions. If the phone forgot its pairing, explicitly pass
  `{"reset":true}` to disconnect the old session and show a fresh code. Reset refuses pending approvals;
  answer or cancel them first. Concurrent calls join the same attempt, and failures release all waiters.

## When to use it

Call `request_approval` before any high-stakes or irreversible action a human should sign off on:
spending money, deploying, deleting or modifying data, granting access, sending external communications,
or any judgment call you are not authorized to make alone. Treat anything other than an explicit approval
(declined, timed out, error) as "do not proceed".

## Security model

- End-to-end encrypted — plaintext only ever exists on your machine and the human's phone.
- Content-blind relay — forwards ciphertext verbatim; it cannot read or forge approvals, and holds
  rooms in memory. Paired peers can reconnect after a relay restart. Restarting the local agent loses
  its in-memory pairing keys and requires re-pairing; the phone persists its pairing in browser storage.
- Pairing is a SPAKE2-style handshake — an in-house construction following RFC 9382 over the ristretto255
  group (RFC 9496). A short code (delivered out-of-band, typed into the app) becomes a strong shared key with no
  relay-in-the-middle. App traffic is then sealed with NaCl secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305).
- The MCP server runs on your machine; it and the phone hold the keys and plaintext. It never auto-approves.

- Upgrade from 0.1.x and physical iPhone checks: https://github.com/askahuman/askahuman/blob/main/docs/releases/0.2.0.md

Approval protocol v2 signs the full question, exact typed answer, and agent acceptance receipt. Both signing identities are authenticated during pairing. The phone confirms receipt only after verifying the agent signature; lost receipts remain uncertain. An answer receipt does not claim an external action executed. Older saved pairings require an updated agent, refreshed phone app, and start_pairing with {"reset":true}. WebCrypto and IndexedDB are required; there is no unsigned fallback. Requests and encoded size are validated before pairing. Text is preserved exactly without trimming, including an explicit text:"" result for empty text; deadlines do not restart after reconnect or reload. Signed request/subscription sequences and atomic per-pair IndexedDB counters reject older recorded state across tabs and reloads. Missing sequence storage requires re-pairing; transport suppression remains possible.
